activityGoals.name: Rotating the Array Values to the Left by One Position
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that has a method that receives an array of values and returns the array rotated to the left by 1 position so that the value at the front of the array goes to the back and the order of the other values stays the same. For example, if the array is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, the program will change it to {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1}.

lineList.content: //Step 1: Define the method for rotating the array to the left by 1 position

commentList: This statement declares the method rotateLeft that takes an array, rotates the array to the left, and returns the rotated array.

lineList.content: //Step 1.1: Store the value at the front in a local variable

commentList:
The value at the front of the array is supposed to go to the back of the array, and the other values are supposed to rotate forward. We can make the task easier by storing the value at the front of the array into a local variable and then shift the other values to the left by one position.

This statement stores the value of the element at index 0 (i.e., value at the front of the array) to the variable first. We will use variable first later to move the value at the front to the back of the array.

lineList.content: //Step 1.2: Rotate the remaining values of the array to the left

commentList:
With value at the front safely tucked away, we now have to shift the remaining values to the left by one position. We could break down the overall task into shifting operations, each of which is a simple assignment statement.

Because of repeated shift operations on the array elements, we’d want to write this with a for loop. We’ll replace element at index i with the value currently stored in the element at index i+1, this will shift value at index i+1 to the left, by one position. We'll put this line of code inside the for loop.

To shift all the remaining elements, we need to iterate through indexes that start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including lst.length-1. Note that we need to terminate the loop when the control variable reaches lst.length-1 because in the assignment statement in the loop body we always move the element one position ahead of the element at the current index.
Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.
We need to shift value at index i+1 to value at index i. We do this by setting the value at index i to the value at index i+1.

lineList.content: //Step 1.3: Move the value at the front to the back of the array

commentList: After shifting the values to the left, we’ve made room at the end of the array for the value that used to be at the front of the array (which is currently stored in a local variable called first). This statement copies the value of variable first to the last element of the array.
Note that lst.length-1 is the index of the last element in the array.
Now that we finished rotating the array elements, we need to return the rotated array. The return statement, when reached, ends the method call and sends the result back to the caller.

commentList: We define this method to print the elements in an int array.

activityGoals.name: Rotating the Array Values to the Right by One Position
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that has a method that receives an array of values and returns the array rotated to the right by one position so that the value that is currently at the end of the array is moved to the front, shifting the remaining values to the right. For example, if the array is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, the program will change it to {6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

lineList.content: //Step 1: Define the method for rotating the array to the right by one position

commentList: This statement declares the method rotateRight that takes an array, rotates the array to the right, and returns the rotated array.

lineList.content: //Step 1.1: Store the value at the end of the array in a local variable

commentList:
The value at the end of the array is supposed to go to the front of the array, and the other values are supposed to rotate backward. We can make the task easier by storing the value at the end of the array into a local variable and then shift the other values to the right by one position.

This statement stores the value of the element at the end of the array that is located at index lst.length-1 to the variable last.
The expression lst.length returns the number of the values in the array. We will use variable last later to move the value at the end to the front of the array.

lineList.content: //Step 1.2: Rotate the remaining elements of the array to the right

commentList:

We could break down the overall task into shifting operations, each of which is a simple assignment statement. Because of repeated shift operations on the array elements, we’d want to write this with a for loop. We’ll replace element at index i with the value currently stored in the element at index i-1, this will shift value at index i-1 to the right, by one position. We'll put this line of code inside the for loop.

To properly shift the elements to the right, we have to run the loop in reverse order (from right to left instead of left to right).

Note that we need to terminate the loop when the control variable reaches 0 because in the assignment statement in the loop body we always move the element one position before the element at the current index. That is, when we get into index 1, we move the element at index 0 to index 1.

We need to shift value at index i-1 to value at index i. We do this by setting the value at index i to the value at index i-1.

activityGoals.name: Rotating the List Values to the Right by Two Position
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that has a function that receives a list of values and returns the list rotated to the right by 2 position so that the value that is currently at the end of the list is moved to the second position, the second last value of the list is moved to the front of the list, and the remaining values are shifted to the right. For example, if the list is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, the program will change it to {5, 6, 1, 2, 3, 4}.
